title: OpenAI Integrates GPT-6.1 Terra into GitHub Copilot to Enable Lower Cost AI Agents
summary:
The GPT-6.1 Terra model is now accessible to developers via OpenRouter and within GitHub Copilot's CLI and app. The model, which OpenAI designed for visual reasoning and "computer use," is intended to automate business workflows by interpreting screen content and taking action across various software applications.

In agentic performance tests, the model solved 50.3% of tasks on the Terminal-Bench 4.0 coding benchmark, compared to 21.5% for the GPT-5.6 Terra version. Its hallucination rate on the AA-Omniscience benchmark fell to 38% from 88%, though GitHub Copilot's early tests found it took more time and tokens to render complex scenes than the previous version. Under its preparedness framework, OpenAI classified the model as "critical" in cybersecurity and "high" for biological and chemical capabilities.

The model is available through the OpenAI API at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, with a 1.05M context window. OpenAI is also adjusting the default power presets in ChatGPT Work for some Plus and Pro users, substituting GPT-6.1 Sol at the "Light" setting with GPT-6.1 Terra at the "Medium" setting.

selectedTweets.text:
OpenAI has released GPT-6.1 Terra, pushing the cost efficiency frontier. It is the first Terra-class model since GPT-5.6, and is more intelligent for less than a third of the cost

Pricing per token is half or less that of GPT-5.6 Terra - at $1/$5 per million input/output tokens vs $2/$12 for the previous model. Cache write has also halved, now at $1.25 per million tokens. Cached input is one quarter at $0.05 vs $0.20 per million tokens.

Key takeaways:

➤ Pareto-optimal for Intelligence vs Cost at low and medium effort: At max effort, GPT-6.1 Terra gains 6 points in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index over GPT-5.6 Terra, at less than a third of the cost per task ($0.40 vs $1.40). At lower effort levels the gain is larger, between 7 and 13 points. The low and medium effort levels are Pareto-optimal for cost efficiency, while the other effort levels sit behind the frontier. At max effort, the model scores 4 points below GPT-6.1 Sol and 10 points above GPT-6 Luna in the Intelligence Index.

➤ Pushes the Coding Agent Index cost efficiency frontier: With a score of 48 in the newly released Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v2.0, the model is 6 points below GPT-6.1 Sol (54) and 17 points above GPT-6 Luna (31). The xhigh and low effort settings sit on the frontier of cost efficiency in the Coding Agent Index, while other effort levels are behind the frontier.

➤ 50 point drop in hallucination rate: GPT-6.1 Terra guesses 38% of the time when it does not know the answer to a question in AA-Omniscience, our private knowledge and hallucination benchmark. Previously, GPT-5.6 Terra's hallucination rate was 88%. This significant reduction in hallucination is coupled with a 2 point increase in AA-Omniscience accuracy - meaning the model simultaneously answers more questions correctly.

➤ 20 point jump in Terminal-Bench 4.0, small improvements across most evaluations: The model makes significant progress in the terminal-based agentic benchmark, Terminal-Bench 4.0, with a gain of ~20 points, now rivaling GPT-6.1 Sol at max effort. Gains across most other evaluations are smaller, for example, 5 points in GDP.pdf.

Congratulations @OpenAI and @sama on the launch!

selectedTweets.bestBit: Cut $200 ChatGPT Pro Codex allowance from 20x to 10x Plus this Friday (Oct 30).
selectedTweets.text:
Look at what OpenAI quietly buried in today's ChatGPT release notes for GPT-6.1 Terra:

"Some Plus and Pro users may see GPT-6.1 Terra at Medium instead of GPT-6.1 Sol at Light in the default Power presets in Work."

Now connect the three moves from this week:
1. Cut API token cost to $1/$5 (half the price of 6.1 Sol, 1/10th of GPT-6 Astra).
2. Quietly swap Plus and Pro default presets from 6.1 Sol to 6.1 Terra.
3. Cut $200 ChatGPT Pro Codex allowance from 20x to 10x Plus this Friday (Oct 30).

GPT-6.1 Terra was not built to beat Claude Opus 5.5. It was built to save OpenAI's margin on $200 Pro accounts.

selectedTweets.bestBit: GPT-6.1 Terra took almost 4x longer and used 48% more tokens, but it still came out 38% cheaper
selectedTweets.text:
GPT-6.1 Terra is out, and @OpenAI's launch demo builds a tram in Lisbon. We stayed in Lisbon for our own test.

We asked GPT-6.1 Terra and GPT-5.6 Terra to recreate Belém Tower at golden hour: the 16th-century limestone fortress on the Tagus, with carved stone rope details, open balconies, battlements, and domed turrets. We also asked for seagulls, a passing sailboat, and the 25 de Abril Bridge in the haze.

GPT-6.1 Terra took almost 4x longer and used 48% more tokens, but it still came out 38% cheaper, at $0.047 vs $0.077, due to its price per token being less than half of 5.6's.

That extra time shows up on screen. 6.1 built the actual tower, with stacked arched windows, domed corner turrets, and sunlight glaring off the Tagus. Its page is 31% larger, and it renders the scene in 432 separate pieces per frame vs 323.

While GPT-5.6 Terra still covered the basics, with domed turrets, a balcony ring, a sailboat, and seagulls, its tower is a simpler, blockier shape with only a few arched openings. Its water is flat, with no golden-hour reflections, and the 25 de Abril Bridge is just two bare posts in the haze.

Try both models now and judge for yourself on https://t.co/5Bc9iiaXyc!
